Two test projects running different xunit major-minor versions can produce subtly different test behaviors (e.g., xunit 2.8.x changed assertion semantics). One project is a full major release behind on the runner. This is a correctness risk.

**Fix:** Unify via Central Package Management. Pin all test infra to the latest tested versions.

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns to fix)

### W1. No Central Package Management (`Directory.Packages.props`)

All 5 projects manage their own `Version=` attributes. With only 5 projects the pain is manageable, but you already have 3 drift instances. CPM eliminates this class of bug entirely.

**Fix:** Create `Directory.Packages.props` at the repo root:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Shared -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Swashbuckle.AspNetCore" Version="6.5.0" />
    <!-- Test -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.10.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Then remove every `Version="…"` attribute from every `<PackageReference>` in all `.csproj` files.

### W2. Massive property duplication — no `Directory.Build.props`

These 7 properties appear identically in **all 5** project files:

```
TargetFramework, Nullable, ImplicitUsings, TreatWarningsAsErrors,
EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, Company, Authors
```

That's 35 duplicated lines. Any policy change (e.g., upgrading to `net9.0`) requires editing 5 files — a recipe for partial upgrades.

**Fix:** Create `Directory.Build.props` at the repo root:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Test project defaults -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

Then delete these 7 properties (plus `IsPackable`) from every `.csproj`.

### W3. Duplicated `DocumentationFile` + `PrintBuildInfo` target — no `Directory.Build.targets`

All 3 source projects repeat the same `DocumentationFile` property and the identical `PrintBuildInfo` target. This is 12 duplicated lines.

**Fix:** Create `Directory.Build.targets` at the repo root:

```xml
<Project>
  <!-- Generate XML docs for non-test projects -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build"
          Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
  </Target>
</Project>
```

Then remove the `<DocumentationFile>` PropertyGroup and the `<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo">` from all 3 source `.csproj` files.

### W4. `PrintBuildInfo` target has no `Inputs`/`Outputs`

The `PrintBuildInfo` target runs on every build unconditionally. While it's just a `<Message>` task today (no real cost), the missing `Inputs`/`Outputs` pattern means it can never be skipped during incremental builds. If heavier logic is added later, this will silently break incrementality.

**Fix:** Since this is purely informational, adding `Condition="'$(BuildingInsideVisualStudio)' != 'true'"` would at least suppress it during IDE builds where the message goes unnoticed. If it ever does real work, add proper `Inputs`/`Outputs`.

### W5. `xunit.runner.visualstudio` should have `PrivateAssets="all"`

Both test projects reference `xunit.runner.visualstudio` without `PrivateAssets="all"`. This is a test-infrastructure-only package that should never flow to consuming projects. The SDK doesn't automatically restrict it.

**Fix:** In both test `.csproj` files (or centrally once CPM is adopted):
```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" PrivateAssets="all" />
```

Similarly, `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` should also get `PrivateAssets="all"`.

### S1. Split PropertyGroups in source projects

In Core, Services, and Api the properties are split across two `<PropertyGroup>` blocks (main + `DocumentationFile`). Once `DocumentationFile` moves to `Directory.Build.targets`, each `.csproj` should have a single, clean `<PropertyGroup>` — this will happen naturally from the consolidation above.

### S2. Consider `GenerateDocumentationFile` instead of `DocumentationFile`

The modern SDK property is:
```xml
<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
```
This automatically sets the `DocumentationFile` to the correct path. Using the raw `DocumentationFile` property works, but `GenerateDocumentationFile` is more idiomatic in SDK-style projects and handles edge cases (e.g., `OutputPath` changes) automatically.

### S3. Api project may not need explicit `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

`Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` is a transitive dependency of the ASP.NET Core framework (it's included in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App`). The explicit `PackageReference` in the Api project is redundant for the web host and may cause version pinning conflicts with the framework bundle.

**Recommendation:** Remove the explicit reference from Api unless the project targets a version different from the framework bundle.

### S4. Consider solution folders in `.sln`

The solution file has all 5 projects at the root level. Adding `src` and `test` solution folders would mirror the disk layout and improve IDE navigation.
